instructions: Unroll the tofu skin and rinse it under cold water. Drain it well and cut it into ribbons about 1/4 inch wide. If yours comes pre-cut, just rinse and drain it.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks. Thinly slice the scallions and chop the cilantro.
Grate the ginger and mince the garlic. In a large bowl, whisk them with the vinegar, soy sauce, maple syrup and sesame oil.
Add the tofu skin, cucumber and carrot to the bowl. Toss until everything is coated in the dressing.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more vinegar or soy sauce.
Top with the scallions, cilantro and sesame seeds. Serve with the chili oil at the table.
To pack it for lunch, keep the dressing in a jar and the tofu skin and vegetables in a box. Toss them together when you're ready to eat.
method_notes: The lead is Okonomi Kitchen's spicy tofu skin salad: tofu skin ribbons with cucumber and carrot in a black vinegar, soy, ginger and garlic dressing with a little sesame oil, scaled from 2 to 4. Chloe Ting's version uses the same vinegar, soy and sesame oil with peanut butter, which was left out (nut-free). The lead's lao gan ma chili crisp and peanut garnish are replaced by plain chili oil at the table and sesame seeds. The lead has only 6 ratings, so this is a fallback lead. Check the tofu skin package: if it says to blanch it first, boil it for 1 minute and cool it before step 2.
